fatal_errors: The proposed 900–1000 K anneal is not demonstrably sub-crystallization; amorphous transition-metal–phosphorus ribbons crystallize on reheating far below the liquid-solid transformation temperatures used to justify this window. The target ribbon begins devitrifying at 659 K and finishes near 820 K, so 950 K would crystallize rather than stabilize it.

The hypothesis misses the target intervention: changing Fe/Co/Mn ratios and reducing phosphorus to 15 at.% to suppress primary phases and favor eutectic solidification, followed by melt spinning at 40 m/s.
The cited evidence establishes cooling-rate-dependent amorphization but provides no support for post-quench annealing, elimination of crystalline embryos, or an upward crystallization-onset shift.

The proposed mechanism assumes structural relaxation reduces nucleation sites, although annealing metallic glasses near or above crystallization can instead promote diffusion, phase separation, and phosphide nucleation.
explanation: The response addresses amorphous retention and supplies a controlled DSC/XRD/TEM test, but it neither reconstructs the compositional intervention nor respects the relevant thermal boundaries. It confuses high-temperature solidification arrests with the reheating crystallization onset of an amorphous ribbon. Consequently, the specified 950 K treatment would likely cause extensive devitrification. The evidence supports rapid-quench amorphization of the original alloy only, not the annealing mechanism or predicted stabilization. The experiment is reasonably discriminating in form, although its arbitrary >50 K criterion could reject smaller genuine effects.
